subject: Chemistry
title: Uses of Aldehydes and Ketones: From Formalin to Vanilla
summary: Where aldehydes and ketones turn up in daily life: formalin and Bakelite from formaldehyde, acetic acid from acetaldehyde, acetone as a solvent, and vanillin, cinnamaldehyde and benzaldehyde as smells and flavours, each explained from its C=O group.
keyPoints: **Formaldehyde** (HCHO): **formalin** (~40% in water) preserves specimens; it also makes **Bakelite** and urea–formaldehyde glues.
HCHO is the most reactive carbonyl compound: **no alkyl group** pushes electrons into, or crowds, its C=O carbon.
**Acetone** and ethyl methyl ketone are **solvents**: a polar C=O (O δ⁻, C δ⁺) plus non-polar CH₃ groups.
**Acetaldehyde** is a starting material: oxidation gives **acetic acid**; also ethyl acetate, polymers and drugs.
**Vanillin** (vanilla), **cinnamaldehyde** (cinnamon) and **benzaldehyde** (almond; perfumes and dyes) each carry a **benzene ring + CHO**.

blocks.p: Formaldehyde reacts with the –NH₂ groups of proteins and joins the chains through **–CH₂– bridges**. The tissue is fixed, and microbes cannot decompose it; formaldehyde also kills them.

list: In base, phenol becomes **phenoxide**; a lone pair on O⁻ moves into the ring.
The ring's C=C π bond at the **ortho** carbon attacks the carbon of HCHO.
The **C=O π pair** of HCHO moves onto its oxygen.
After proton transfers the ring carries **–CH₂OH**; repeated, –CH₂– bridges join rings into **Bakelite**, a hard cross-linked plastic.

sections.h: Why acetone is a good solvent

blocks.p: The **C=O** group is polar (O δ⁻, C δ⁺), so acetone mixes with water. Its two **CH₃** groups are non-polar, so it also dissolves oils, paints and grease: one molecule, both kinds of solvent power.

quiz.q: Formalin, used to preserve biological specimens, is an aqueous solution of:
quiz.explain: Formalin is about 40% formaldehyde (HCHO) in water.

quiz.q: Bakelite is a polymer of phenol and:
quiz.explain: Phenol–formaldehyde resin: –CH₂– bridges join the rings.

quiz.q: Why is formaldehyde the most reactive carbonyl compound?
options: it has no alkyl group on the C=O carbon
quiz.explain: No alkyl group donates electrons to, or crowds, its carbonyl carbon.

quiz.q: Acetone dissolves both water and oils because it has:
options: a polar C=O and non-polar CH₃ groups
quiz.explain: The polar C=O mixes with water; the CH₃ groups dissolve non-polar substances.

quiz.q: Vanillin, cinnamaldehyde and benzaldehyde all contain:
options: a benzene ring and a CHO group
quiz.explain: Each is an aromatic aldehyde: a ring carrying –CHO.

simulation.reason: A real-life applications topic: the uses are facts tied to one structural idea each (reactive HCHO, polar plus non-polar acetone, ring + CHO), which the video, the table and the quiz carry. There is no variable to manipulate.
